impactStories.label: Water
impactStories.title: Water accounting and hydrology
impactStories.summary: Landsat is a backbone dataset for monitoring reservoirs, surface-water extent, snow and ice patterns, water quality, and irrigation water use. Thermal measurements are especially important for evapotranspiration and drought assessment.
impactStories.story: From irrigation districts to river basins, Landsat helps convert imagery into decisions about consumptive water use, crop stress, reservoir conditions, and changing hydrologic patterns.

impactStories.label: Forests
impactStories.title: Forests, biomass, and carbon
impactStories.summary: Because Landsat has been observing land for more than five decades, it is one of the strongest tools for tracking deforestation, recovery, disturbance history, and forest productivity over time.
impactStories.story: Landsat shows where forest change happened and when; GEDI adds the missing 3D structure. Together they support biomass, habitat, and sustainable forest management applications.

impactStories.label: Agriculture
impactStories.title: Agriculture and food systems
impactStories.summary: Landsat supports crop condition assessment, acreage tracking, field-scale land management, and water-use monitoring. Moderate-resolution thermal data makes it unusually powerful for agricultural stress detection.

metrics.label: Typical cadence
metrics.value: 8-day Landsat pair or faster with HLS

impactStories.story: Landsat helps move agricultural monitoring beyond color imagery toward energy balance, evapotranspiration, and crop stress signals that matter operationally.

impactStories.label: Cities
impactStories.title: Urban heat and built environments
impactStories.summary: Thermal bands reveal how cities retain heat, while optical bands show expansion, impervious surfaces, vegetation loss, and neighborhood-scale environmental inequity patterns.
impactStories.story: Landsat provides repeatable heat-island context over decades, which is critical for planning cooling infrastructure, greening strategies, and heat-risk interventions.

impactStories.label: Hazards
impactStories.title: Wildfire, floods, and environmental disturbance
impactStories.summary: Landsat supports burn severity mapping, recovery monitoring, flood extent interpretation, and broader land disturbance analysis with a record long enough to show whether a current event is exceptional or part of a trend.
impactStories.story: For hazards, Landsat is often the archive that anchors event context, recovery trajectories, and long-term land-change baselines.

complementaryMissions.name: Sentinel-2
complementaryMissions.short: Adds more frequent Landsat-like optical coverage at 10 to 20 m scales.
complementaryMissions.detail: NASA's HLS project harmonizes Landsat 8/9 with Sentinel-2A/B/C to create analysis-ready surface reflectance with a global median repeat under 1.4 days in 2025.

complementaryMissions.name: ECOSTRESS
complementaryMissions.short: Adds detailed thermal insight into plant temperature and evapotranspiration.
complementaryMissions.detail: ECOSTRESS measures plant temperature from the International Space Station and helps quantify evapotranspiration and water stress, complementing Landsat's broader, stable land record.

complementaryMissions.name: SWOT
complementaryMissions.short: Adds water-surface elevation and changing surface-water geometry.
complementaryMissions.detail: SWOT provides the first global survey of Earth's surface water elevation, giving hydrologists information that pairs naturally with Landsat's water extent and land-context observations.

complementaryMissions.name: GEDI
complementaryMissions.short: Adds vertical forest structure and biomass context.
complementaryMissions.detail: GEDI measures the 3D structure of forests from lidar on the ISS. Landsat shows disturbance history across space and time; GEDI adds canopy height and structural detail.
